agent.about: Harbor 0.21.0 on tbench (/home/ubuntu/harbor-env, its files verified against the wheel RECORD by the tbench preflight), the built-in Terminus 2 (`-a terminus-2`, harbor.agents.terminus_2:Terminus2, version 2.0.0) unchanged: json parser, its prompt template, summarization on (threshold 8000), its own retries (LiteLLM.call 3 x, _query_llm 3 x; the server must answer a re-sent request deterministically), no session header and no close (the runtime binds a session by its first message). The job config (controller.harbor_job_config, rendered on DeltaAI from this section and sent with the run) sets: the dataset at its pinned ref (the plan's task names as the filter), n_concurrent_trials 16 (agent.n_concurrent, at most the servers' K), n_attempts 1, timeout multiplier 1.0 (the task timeouts unchanged: build-pov-ray 12,000 s, sam-cell-seg 7,200 s), Harbor's own trial retries off (max_retries 0), quiet, the docker environment with delete, verification on; the agent kwargs: api_base = the loopback relay of the job's tunnel, model_info, temperature 0, llm_kwargs (max_tokens 4096, litellm timeout 3600 s so that a request waiting in the server's admission is not cancelled and re-sent, no litellm / OpenAI-client retries). Thinking off: our runtime renders the thinking-off generation header itself; the stock control gets enable_thinking false from the client per call (stock.llm_call_kwargs, as SWE-bench). HARBOR_TELEMETRY=0 on every harbor process.

budget.about: Seconds reserved per job and per server (controller.plan_fit; at run time the harbor cap is min(plan cap, what the deadline leaves)), perf-swe32's measured reserves: job checks 60, server start to READY 360, tunnel 60, stop 180 (stop_harbor.sh: SIGTERM, Harbor cancels its trials and removes their containers, harbor_stop_timeout_seconds 150), checks 300 (89 sessions of ~5-25 calls each, about the swe16 runs' turns), finish 480 (closes, S2, RECORD, the xz archives), margin 300; the stock control: checks 120, finish 180. R = 1,740 s (ours) / 1,260 s (stock). eval_wait (per plan): a SWE evaluation (565-574 s for 32 instances) may hold a shared lock when a job starts; the job waits up to 600 s from its start (overlapping the server start) and refuses cleanly at the bound.
budget.stall_about: The job's stall watchdog during each Harbor run (job.StallWatchdog): every stall_poll_seconds it reads the server's pending requests (runtime: GET /v1/chat-text/info, client sessions busy plus sessions waiting to open; stock: vLLM running + waiting), its completed rows (runtime.jsonl) and vLLM's prompt / generation token counters; when requests are pending and nothing completed and no token was computed for stall_watchdog_seconds it records CAPACITY_STALL (capacity-stall-<label>.json), stops the Harbor run (stop_harbor.sh) and the server FAILs, so a pool that cannot hold one more turn ends the run instead of burning the allocation. It only shortens a run: the time plan is unchanged.

config.plans_about: One ghx4 batch job per configuration (1 GPU, --mem=113560M, billing 1000 = one GPU-hour per hour), all 89 tasks, 16 concurrent trials. Time limit = 1.3 x E rounded up to the minute, E = the expected elapsed = the measured reserves (~1,100 s ours, ~700 s stock) + the expected harbor wall W = 12,800 s: the two August Terminus jobs' trials (n = 8, thinking on) rescheduled at n = 16 in Harbor's order give 12,032 / 13,235 s, set by build-pov-ray's 12,000-s agent timeout (it starts in the first wave and timed out in both runs); every trial at its agent timeout + 120 s gives 13,980 s (+ 300 s: 14,850 s). Harbor cap = limit - every reserve (>= the all-timeout schedule); harbor minimum = 12,600 s (build-pov-ray's timeout + 600 s; with less left after the lock wait the job refuses before any agent). One run per job: a cut run is TB16_PARTIAL and gives no throughput. D:/Remote-RA-temp/scratch/perf-tb16/make_tasks.py -> tb16-sizing.json. dry: the optional first GPU contact (full then observation_query, 16 tasks with 900-s timeouts, the dry subset). goal (2026-10-21): goal_query on the 89 tasks (Table 1 Ours), the same time as full / obs / rfill; goaldry / goaldryi: goal_query on the dry subset (ghx4 batch / ghx4-interactive), dryo's time. ggoal / ggoaldry: the Gemma goal_query plans (integrate-1021 9ef0d6d, explicit T = 20,480); gobsdry / grfilldry: observation_query / random_fill alone on the Gemma dry subset (2026-10-22), ggoaldry's time. ctx25 / ctx24 (2026-10-26): the 262,144-token Qwen dry plans at the group's settings, goal_query then observation_query on the dry subset in one job with their own server settings (plans.<name>.server: KV 25 / 24 GiB, --max-model-len 262144, --dram-arena-gib 70) and arena sizing (plans.<name>.memory); ctx25 blocked by the sealed Qwen KV sizes (kv_block), ctx24 submittable; dryi's time.

selection.about: THE KV budget of the three selective policies (observation_query, random_fill, goal_query): serve.py --active-token-budget N, a fixed per-session token budget (the same for the three; full and stock have none). The value is to be agreed (user decision 2026-10-16: configurable); 8192 is the SWE-bench value. The runtime's selection starts only once a session's sealed history exceeds its switch threshold (8,192 tokens; pinned from the sealed source), and the August Terminus runs' largest prompt per trial had a median of about 9.1K tokens, so on TB many trials stay below it with any budget. Changing it: edit this one value, build.py --reuse-bundle, local_validation.ps1 (the phrases and times do not change).

server.about: Shared by every server of our runtime (full, observation_query, random_fill, goal_query): serve.py flags. K = max_running_sessions = 20 open sessions per server (vLLM max_num_seqs), Harbor -n 16 (agent.n_concurrent; the stock control runs max_num_seqs = -n): the 4 spares take finished trials (Terminus sends no close) and Terminus's summary sub-calls (the user, 2026-10-16; INTERFACE.md of tb-runtime 0fd34f3: a chat-text server runs up to 24, sessions.py MAX_CHAT_TEXT_RUNNING). max_model_len 65536 = THE TB context, one value (build.py gives the stock control's max_model_len and Terminus's model_info.max_input_tokens this value): the August runs' model_info (a prompt plus its reply must fit; Terminus summarizes when fewer than 8000 tokens are left and handles the context-limit 400); at K = 20 and 32 GiB, 131072 does not fit the no-deadlock rule; PROVISIONAL; max_tokens 4096, the reply bound (Terminus sends llm_kwargs.max_tokens 4096 too). dram_arena_gib 64 (INTERFACE.md section 1: 65,536 Pages of 1 MiB, e.g. 20 sessions of 52K tokens; 67.9 GiB pinned with the pool and the carries; the arena of every session at the limit would be 80.3 GiB, 84.1 GiB pinned, which does not fit --mem=113560M with the 32-GiB reserve): a capture beyond it fails that request with DRAM_ARENA_EXHAUSTED (a failure in the checks). connector_pool_gib 1, the optimized runtime (the user, 2026-10-21: Table 1 runs with the optimized flags): decode_fastpath, decode_fastpath2 and decode_fastpath3 true (serve.py refuses 3 without 2 and 2 without 1) and deferred_completion_io true (the completion files written off the engine thread), language_model_only true (the startup spike ELIMINATED); the Gemma servers keep decode_fastpath alone (config.gemma.server: the Gemma 4 profile refuses --decode-fastpath3 and --deferred-completion-io; its plans keep their flags). protocol: the runtime's chat protocol for Terminus 2 (`chat_text_v1`: the serve.py --protocol value, its extra arguments and the session binding are read from the sealed source by controller.chat_text_feature and pinned in pins.json runtime_features.chat_text).
server.optimized_about: The optimized runtime of the paper's Table 1 (the user, 2026-10-21): --decode-fastpath --decode-fastpath2 --decode-fastpath3 --deferred-completion-io --language-model-only on every Qwen runtime server (full, observation_query, random_fill, goal_query); each switch pins its startup key (startup.json, READY; the decode fast paths also the worker receipt) and changes no vLLM argument (release parity: the vLLM command equals the one without them). Accepted on chat-text for every policy by the sealed serve.py (test_release_parity) and by the runtime's CPU end-to-end evidence (runtime_evidence.py: test_integrate_flags' chat-text runs with the three fast paths, test_deferred_completion's chat-text server). Not GPU-validated on TB before these runs.
server.protocol_about: INTERFACE.md (tb-runtime 0fd34f3) section 1: --protocol chat-text (chat_text_v1, no --task), its slots over the lifetime (client sessions + summarization calls + rebinds; 512 = the runtime's default, at least 128 required), and the close rule: failed / rebound / client-closed / bound-reached slots close at once; a live session closes only when all K are open: for each request waiting to open, the least recently used one idle >= --chat-text-evict-after (30 s) closes, asides first; with nobody waiting, the least recently used one idle >= --chat-text-idle-timeout (600 s) closes, one, so the next new session finds a spare. The runtime's defaults, pinned explicitly (PROVISIONAL).
server.release_about: --release-idle-pages on every runtime server (coordinator, 2026-10-17, after job 3398129: full at K = 20 / 32 GiB / 65,536 without it pinned 26,632 of 26,698 FA blocks with 16 idle sessions; a turn admitted while nothing ran found no block and vLLM preempted it, which aborts the EngineCore). Under GPU pressure the capacity gate releases idle sessions' resident Pages, least recently used first (their DRAM copies stay in the arena's catalog: no new pinned host memory) and readmits them before the session's next turn; with 68d19b4 a turn that still does not fit waits (CAPACITY_WAIT) instead of running. Evidence: capacity.jsonl (evict / readmit), the rows' and native files' idle_release, engine-cleanup.json totals; a preemption stays a failure.

stock.about: Same-node stock vLLM 0.24.0 control (as perf-swe32): plain vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server from the reused clean env, no runtime source, the same context (server.max_model_len, given by build.py), reply bound and KV bytes, max_num_seqs = Harbor's -n (16), prefix caching, --gdn-prefill-backend triton, VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0, vLLM's own --language-model-only; served under the same model name. vLLM's default chat template kwargs on the server (the user, 2026-10-16: as SWE-bench); thinking off comes from the client per call (llm_call_kwargs: extra_body.chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false, Terminus 2's per-call LiteLLM kwargs), so the stock job config differs from ours by that one entry. Greedy from the client's temperature 0; replies end at EOS or at max_tokens (finish_reason length, which Terminus handles).

stock_thinking.about: The thinking-on stock control of the thinking plans (perf-tb16-strip, strip25): config.stock with these keys over it and the plan's own context and KV size (controller.stock_section: kv_cache_gib, max_model_len of config.plans.<name>.server). The client sends the stock default template with thinking on per call (llm_call_kwargs extra_body.chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking true, no preserve_thinking: every past reply renders as its content only, the strip servers' history); vLLM's Qwen3 reasoning parser (--reasoning-parser qwen3) returns the text after </think> as the content and the reasoning apart, as our strip servers return it, and Harbor 0.21.0's Terminus 2 (interleaved_thinking off, harbor/llms/chat.py) sends back the content only. Everything else is config.stock's (vLLM's defaults: CUDA graphs, async scheduling, prefix caching, max_num_seqs = Harbor's -n). tbench_host.about: tbench/bin/host_check.py (the login-node preflight; run_harbor.sh after taking the locks): refuses only for leftover containers of OUR previous runs (the docker compose projects of our trials: <trial>__env and its verifier projects) and for MemAvailable / free disk below these limits; other containers (the SWE halves, other users' Harbor work) and the load are reported, never refused; nothing that is not ours is ever stopped or removed. shared_lock_roots: the tbench lock is shared with the SWE harnesses: a TB run takes its own lock (/home/ubuntu/tb16/lock) and each SWE half's lock through a byte-identical copy of that half's lock module (perf-gemma0's way with swe16's), so a SWE pool, stress test or evaluation never runs beside a TB run and the other way round; a running SWE evaluation is waited for (bounded, eval_wait_seconds). tbench: 16 vCPU, 30 GB RAM, -n 16 trials with 2-8 GB memory limits.

tbench_verify.about: 2026-11-12 (perf-swe32's evidence push of 2026-11-11, ported): after its archives the job pushes fetch/tb16-core.tar.xz and tb16-bulk.tar.xz to <root>/evidence/<run_id>/ over its tbench SSH link (one ssh per archive, stdin to a .part file, SHA-256 checked against archives.json on arrival before the rename, never over a different file) and calls <root>/code/by-payload/<payload members id> -> code/<tag>/tbench_verify/remote_verify.py trigger (the code tree postrun/verify_on_tbench.py --deploy installed; checked against its SHA256SUMS): it records the job's archive SHA-256 values and end record (status, the Slurm state it implies: from the job, confirmed by the END mail) and starts a detached niced waiter that verifies once the evidence is complete and the run's Harbor runs ended (bin/package_run.sh's rule; at most wait_seconds): verify_evidence, the tbench run package, join_tb16 and tb16_tables as postrun/fetch_run.ps1 runs them, writing out/<run_id>/RESULT.json; verify_on_tbench.py --pull (with the END mail's Slurm state and exit code) brings the small result home. Best effort: at most total_seconds (and never closer than slurm_margin_seconds to the plan's Slurm limit), every ssh with a timeout; any failure is recorded in fetch/tbench-push.json and the job's last line, never in its status; fetch_run.ps1 still works. 2026-11-15: the payload id selects the verification code tree (code/by-payload/<payload members id>), so a change of the tbench verification gets a new payload id and a queued job keeps the code of its own payload (smokeqt 3586720 of payload 98a149cd: perf-tb16-strip-98a149cd). From this payload on the join accepts the killed in-flight row of job 3560498 as a counted finding (KILLED_IN_FLIGHT): the one row beyond the calls of a trial the client killed (AgentTimeoutError) with nothing counted beyond its trajectory, the trial's last row and its session's, its prompt extending the previous row's, the other rows equal to the calls (join_tb16.killed_in_flight_row); every other count difference still fails.
